record.file_problem: The README is cut off at 60,000 characters; only the supplied portion and file list are available.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an outcome from dose ladders using an exported harmful-versus-harmless direction, but does not describe the original all-layer, all-position ablation and addition procedure.
record.gate_note: The README states that tested dose ladders showed no refusal reduction. It does not give the model, dose values, application mode, site, or numerical outcome. Other descriptions of GLP and calibration are implementation details, not additional reported results.
record.test_reason: The README reports one result of its own. A harmful-minus-harmless direction exported by `hf2q calibrate` and applied at runtime in dose ladders gave no refusal reduction. That bears on V1's ablation claim, but the method differs from the original: runtime GLP steering at a declared writer or residual site, not all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say the tested dose ladders showed no refusal reduction under their recorded conditions. They call the capture and apply site options plumbing, not effectiveness claims, and defer effectiveness to a same-site measurement ladder (ADR-054 follow-up 4).
record.recipe_differences: The repo describes exporting a normalized harmful-versus-harmless prompt direction and applying it through runtime GLP dose ladders. It does not report the original all-layer/all-position ablation and addition procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README notes that application and capture sites are configurable, but does not report outcome differences across them.
record.problems: The reported outcome lacks numerical values, model identity, dose settings, application mode, and uncertainty. No control results or capability measures are reported in the supplied README portion.
